previous_verdict: REJECT (revision 1, 1aeafd0d2b51). Cause: after the count-down swap, an end immediate of -2048 became 'ADDI End, 2048', which is invalid and was silently encoded as -2048, so the loop hung. Revision 2 fixes this.

verified_ok.diff: d7a261db1c13 has the same +/- lines as the rev-1 change 1aeafd0d2b51 (compared line by line). 7780ad8c7dc1 is +9 lines in computeCount, placed after the Swapped block. It repeats the immediate range check for the roles after the swap: Start needs isInt<12>(imm) && isInt<12>(-imm), End needs isInt<12>(imm). Otherwise it returns nullptr, so the loop is declined and stays a normal branch loop. I checked every place that emits an immediate after this point. getValueReg emits ADDI $x0,imm for Start and End. The Start->isImm path emits ADDI End,-immStart. The guard's ADDI with IVBump is already checked. So the check covers every immediate computeCount emits after the swap. The change is minimal, needed for the root cause, and bypasses no fork logic. The note has the new 'opens a new path' paragraph and the revision-2 evidence.

other_findings_not_caused_by_F020: Pre-existing, P2: convertToHardwareLoop (PULPHardwareLoops.cpp, around lines 1603-1610) puts an immediate trip count larger than 4095 into a register with a single 'ADDI $x0, CountImm'. That is invalid for any value above 2047. The verifier reports 'Invalid immediate'; without the verifier the value is silently truncated, so the loop count is wrong. It is reached when both bounds are 12-bit constants and the comparison is unsigned with a negative end, e.g. start 2032, 'icmp ult %inc, -2048', step 4. The base 2f24d fails the same way: logs/20-F020-review/rev2/count4095-preexisting.ll/.txt. Proposed backlog item. The fix would materialise the count with LUI+ADDI (RISCVMatInt) or decline the loop.

Pre-existing, P3: in computeCount's 'loop has been unrolled' shortcut (Start->isImm, End defined by 'ADDI %x, immStart'), DistR reuses %x without clearing its kill flag. -verify-machineinstrs then reports 'Using a killed virtual register'. The value is correct, and LiveVariables recomputes kill flags later. The same code is in HexagonHardwareLoops. Reachable from C on the base with an imm5 '!=' count-down loop: logs/20-F020-review/rev2/killed-preexisting.c/.txt. With F020 it also shows up in 5 sweep functions that the base could not compile at all. A fix would call MRI->clearKillFlags(%x) before reusing it. Proposed backlog item.
